findings.claim: The new t6 comment explains the 9-versus-6 check with 'Two quick clicks inside one act(): React handles both clicks before it re-renders, so the second click still sees the old checksRun value.' Learners read this comment in the failure code frame, and it is about the batching concept the task teaches. Read as a description of real clicks, it is wrong: in a browser React flushes each discrete click before handling the next, so two real quick clicks re-render in between. There, an updater and a single setChecksRun(checksRun + 3) both show 6 after two clicks. The 9-versus-6 difference exists only because act() batches both dispatches. A learner who fails here with 'Received: 6 checks run' can come away with a wrong model of when React re-renders.
findings.recommendation: Reword the comment so the batching is attributed to the test, not to quick clicking, for example: 'act() lets the test queue both clicks before React re-renders, just as several setter calls in one handler are queued. Only updater functions add up correctly when updates are queued, so this must read 9.'
